column2: req_desc

Missions with an epoch
Create a mission with a name and an ISO 8601 UTC epoch through the API, rejecting bad input with the field errors in API.

Empty mission console
A mission with no parsed samples shows the empty-mission heading and line from Feedback states in place of the lunar disc, on the author console and on the share page.

Storage-confirmed upload
An uploaded capture becomes `stored` only after object storage confirms the object and its SHA-256 matches the declared checksum, and otherwise no pass, object or kept request key remains, as qualified in Business rules.

Duplicate, empty and oversized captures
Reject a second live copy of the same bytes under a different request key, an empty body, a wrong content type and a body over the size limit with the statuses in API.

Upload announcements
Every upload step (uploading, stored, parsed, rejected with its line number, refused) is announced once in the `Upload status` live region, however many attempts the console makes, with the exact copy in Feedback states.

Upload a pass journey
The author creates a mission on the Missions page, picks a capture file, watches the pass go Uploading, Stored and Parsed in the passes list, and sees its ground track drawn on the disc.

Capture line format
Parse captures under the published line format, including its per-line byte limit, field lengths and byte-order-mark rule, ignoring comment and blank lines but counting them in line numbers.

Parse outcome
A stored pass becomes `parsed` only when every line parses and its search documents are confirmed or recorded as pending, and otherwise becomes `rejected` with the first bad line number and its reason code, within the parse budget in Business rules.

Derived values
Latitude, longitude, altitude above the mean lunar radius, speed and the mission perilune are computed once on the server from SI samples and never change when display units change.

Mission elapsed time
Every sample, transcript line and event carries a server-computed MET in seconds and its label, with pre-epoch times labelled with a T- prefix.

Loupe lens and readout
On pointer enter or touch start with a visible sample within 24 CSS pixels, or on keyboard focus, the lens grows to 160 by 160 CSS pixels at the nearest such sample (the current sample for keyboard focus), stays closed when no sample is that close, and shows the track magnified with a crosshair, while the readout plate shows that sample's lines as listed in Public screens and controls.

Keyboard stepping
The track canvas is a slider named `Track loupe` whose arrow, Shift+arrow, Home and End keys move the lens by one sample, by 60 samples or to the ends, with value text naming MET and altitude.

Moment links
Releasing the pointer, lifting a finger, ending a key step, going to a GMT time, pausing or ending playback, or picking a line or result writes `t=<MET seconds>` to the address while keeping its other parameters, and opening such an address places the lens on the sample at or before that MET.

Current transcript line
The transcript line at or before the lens MET becomes the current line and scrolls into view, and picking any transcript line moves the lens to the sample at or before it.

Touch and reduced motion
On a phone one finger drags the lens along the track without scrolling the page, and with reduced motion the lens appears at full size and numerals change in place while every other loupe behaviour stays the same.

Unit conversion and rounding
Altitude, speed, landmark range, residual and position are displayed under the exact factors and half-away-from-zero rounding of exact half-way values, identically on the readout plate, the Events table, the share page, the event list download and the dossier.

Saved display units
The author's distance and speed unit choice is saved on the mission and becomes the share page's starting units unless the share address names others, while a reader's choice changes only their own view and address.

Channel drawer
Below 1280 pixels wide the channel rail is a drawer, and while it is closed none of its radios or checkboxes is visible, focusable or exposed to assistive technology.

Switch units journey
The author opens the channel drawer on a tablet and switches to nmi and ft/s, and the readout, the Events table and a freshly opened share page all show the same converted values.

Pin events
Pinning an event requires a request key and a MET in whole seconds, snaps the event to the sample at or before that MET, and stores a public title and an optional private note, as qualified in API.

Pin an event by keyboard
Pressing Enter on the track loupe opens the `Pin event` dialog with focus in Title, Tab wraps inside it, Escape cancels it, one opening of the dialog creates at most one event, and focus returns to the loupe after saving or cancelling.

Private notes stay private
A private note appears only in the author console's Note column and Pin event dialog, in author event responses and in the author dossier, never in any share, stream, search, CSV, share dossier, webhook, push alert, audit, title, attribute, storage or header surface listed in Business rules.

Mission-scoped transcript search
Search returns only the mission's transcript lines and public event titles with their MET, never another mission's items, a deleted pass's lines or a landmark.

Latest query wins
The results shown always belong to the text now in the search box, even when an earlier query or refresh answers later.

Search announcements
The `Search status` live region announces the result count for the current query once per search or refresh, with the exact copy in Feedback states.

Jump from a search result
The author types a phrase and picks a result, and the lens, readout, current transcript line and address move to that moment.

Deleted means gone
After a pass is deleted, its samples, transcript lines, events, index entries, pending search writes and stored object are gone from every author view, share view, search and download, its direct URLs answer as gone, and catching up on pending search writes never brings any of them back.

All-or-nothing delete
A pass deletion that cannot reach storage, or whose removal from the index is not confirmed, removes nothing, and of simultaneous deletions of one pass exactly one succeeds.

Keyboard delete confirmation
Deleting a pass asks for confirmation in the `Delete pass` dialog, which works fully from the keyboard and returns focus to the passes list after deleting.

Share link capability
A mission has at most one active unguessable share link, replacing the link kills the old one, and revoking it makes the very next request with it fail.

Read-only replay page
The share page and its API answer only reads, show only parsed passes and public data, are never cached, and refuse every write.

Reader console layouts
The replay console shows one column at 375 pixels wide, the track beside the readout at 768, and the channel rail, track and transcript side by side at 1280 and wider.

Publish and read journey
The author creates a share link with a typed expiry, and a reader opens it on a phone, steps the loupe, searches the transcript and downloads the event list; after the author revokes the link, the reader's next request shows the withdrawn page.

Original capture download
Downloading a capture from the share page or the author console returns the exact uploaded bytes, byte-order mark and comment lines included.

Event list download
The share page's event list download is an RFC 4180 CSV of public events in the reader's current units whose text cells starting with a formula character are neutralised before quoting, as qualified in API.

Capture storage outage
With capture storage unreachable, uploads, deletions and capture downloads on both consoles answer the storage outage status and show the published copy, while the replay still plays.

Storage recovery without restart
When capture storage answers again, the next upload (including a retry under a refused request's key) succeeds without restarting the app and the storage banner clears by itself.

Search outage
With transcript search unreachable, searches and deletions answer the search outage status and the console shows the search banner, while uploads still parse and pins still save.

Search recovery and catch-up
When search answers again, the next search succeeds without a restart, the search banner clears by itself, and lines and titles saved during the outage become searchable, as qualified in Services.

Health and boot
The app answers its health check and serves the consoles even when storage, search, the parse queue, the cache, the PDF renderer, the ephemeris service, billing, webhooks or push alerts are unreachable at start.

Server boundary
The server answers only same-origin app routes, enforces its body limits, answers every error with exactly the keys published for it under one precedence order, and never serves source files or credentials.

Accessible controls
Every public control has its published role and name, is at least 44 by 44 CSS pixels, shows a visible focus mark, and the consoles meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA.

Lunar disc and ground track
The centre pane draws a procedural orthographic lunar disc with a graticule, the ground track, event pins, landmark marks and a perilune mark, legible at every viewport.

Instrument console look
The console reads as a measured, dusty, exact instrument: warm grey ground, hairline rules, tabular mono numerals, an oversized MET readout, and no shadows, rounded cards or pure white.

Real providers and environment credentials
Pass states, parsing, downloads, search, reference vectors, dossiers, rate limits, reader counts, live share updates, plans, webhooks and push alerts come from real calls to the ten services using credentials and URLs read from the environment, never from hard-coded values or secrets held in the browser.

Retry-safe uploads
An upload requires an `Idempotency-Key`, and a retry under the same key replays the first answer without creating a second pass, object or search document, as qualified in Business rules.

Retry-safe event pins
A pin requires an `Idempotency-Key`, and a retry or double press under the same key returns the first event without creating another, as qualified in Business rules.

Bounded parsing
An over-long line, a 50,001st sample or an over-long field rejects the pass at its exact line, and every capture up to the size limit is settled within the parse budget.

Search follows every change
Pins, parsed passes and deletions answer only after the search engine confirms their writes or records them as pending, and a console with a query in its search box re-runs it in place after each change named in Interactions.

Expiring share links
Every share link carries a UTC expiry, by default 30 days after creation, at and after which every share route answers the expired status and an open reader page switches to the expired page, as qualified in Business rules.

Console state survives its timers
Status checks, pass checks, banner changes, pushed updates, reader count changes and track reloads never close a dialog or drawer, move focus, clear the search or a dialog draft, stop playback, or move the lens off its MET, units or address, except where a track reload is said to pause playback.

Server playback frames
The frames API returns the frames on the requested MET grid at 1, 5, 10 or 25 frames per second, each computed by cubic Hermite interpolation between the bracketing samples or held across gaps over 600 seconds, as qualified in API and Business rules.

Play the pass
Play replays the track from the lens sample at 1×, 10× or 60×, timed only by the page's monotonic clock, and every value the readout shows equals the server frame for the playback MET, while reduced motion shows samples without interpolation, as qualified in Interactions.

Mission audit chain
Every mission change appends one audit entry in its own transaction, hash-chained over RFC 8785 canonical JSON and never holding a note, which the audit and verify routes return and check and the share routes never expose.

Reader view in the address
The share page keeps its units, and both consoles keep their search query and moment, in the address under the WHATWG form-urlencoded serialization, so opening that address restores them.

Day-of-year time entry
The `Epoch (GMT)` and `Link expiry (GMT)` fields accept only GMT day-of-year times, refuse anything else in the browser with the published field error and no request, and send the matching ISO instant whatever the browser's time zone.

Instants shown in day-of-year form
The mission epoch in the console header, the share link expiry in the Share region and on the share page, and the readout plate's GMT line show instants in GMT day-of-year form, while every API response keeps ISO instants.

Go to GMT
Entering a GMT day-of-year time in `Go to GMT` on either console moves the lens to the sample at or before that instant, updating the slider, readout and moment link exactly as a key step does.

Pin at a typed MET
The author types a MET label in the Pin event dialog's MET field, the console sends it as whole seconds, and the Events table, share page and API show the event at the sample it snapped to.

Landmark records
The API creates, lists and removes up to five named landmarks per mission in signed decimal degrees, refusing bad names, out-of-range or over-precise coordinates and a sixth landmark with the answers in API.

Landmark coordinate entry
The Latitude and Longitude fields accept decimal degrees with a hemisphere letter or a sign (ASCII hyphen or the Unicode minus sign), refuse anything else in the browser with the published field errors, and send signed decimal degrees.

Landmark ranges and list
Both consoles list the mission's landmarks with formatted coordinates, draw them on the disc, and show one `Range to <name>` readout line per landmark with the great-circle surface distance in the current distance unit.

Mark a landmark journey
The author adds a landmark by typing its name and coordinates, sees it in the list, on the disc and in the readout, and removes it with its `Remove <name>` button from the keyboard.

Mission change stream
Every share link offers an event stream that sends one `mission-changed` event per mission change version, with the version as its event id, across every app instance sharing the database, replays missed versions in order on reconnection with `Last-Event-ID`, and refuses revoked or expired links.

Live reader page
An open share page shows the author's pinned events, parsed or deleted passes, landmark and reference changes, and the withdrawn page after a revocation, within 5 seconds and without a reload, whichever instance each of them uses.

Exact pointer picking
Pointer and touch picks on the disc, including the pick that opens the lens, select the nearest visible sample whose orthographic projection lies within 24 CSS pixels of the pointer, at any device pixel ratio, open or move nothing when none is that close, and centre the lens on that sample's projected point.

Focused controls stay uncovered
Below 1280 pixels the MET band stays pinned at the top and the Events table scrolls inside its own region, and at every viewport no focused or scrolled-to control is partly covered by the band, a drawer, a dialog or the readout plate, except that at 1280 and wider the Track loupe slider is exempt from the plate.

Refused changes leave no trace
A change refused for an outage leaves every row, object, index document, landmark, audit entry and the mission change version untouched and sends no stream message or webhook, while landmark edits and pins still succeed during a search outage.

Author-to-reader replay journey
An author creates a mission, uploads, pins, marks a landmark, sets a reference, switches units and shares on one instance, and a reader on another instance in another time zone checks the same values including the residual, downloads the capture and dossier, appears in the author's reader count, sees a live change and then the withdrawn page.

Verifiable, conditional and range downloads
Every capture download carries a `Repr-Digest` of the full stored representation, every capture and event list download carries a strong `ETag`, HEAD on those routes answers as GET without a body, and capture downloads honour RFC 9110 conditional and single byte-range requests, with the dossier exempt from ETag and Content-Length equality between HEAD and GET, as qualified in API.

UTF-8 capture names
Capture filenames travel percent-encoded as UTF-8, are stored NFC-normalised, appear decoded everywhere, and download with RFC 6266 and RFC 8187 `Content-Disposition` parameters.

Strict JSON in and out
JSON request bodies must be I-JSON, so duplicate member names, unpaired surrogate escapes and integers beyond 2^53 - 1 in magnitude answer `invalid_json`, and every integer in every JSON response is a JSON number, never a string.

Speaker summary
Both consoles list each transcript speaker with its line count, ordered by count and then by code point, treating names such as `__proto__` and `constructor` as ordinary text.

Mission edits as merge patches
Mission edits are RFC 7396 JSON Merge Patch documents in which an absent member stays unchanged and `null` clears the reference target, and the console sends only the members that changed.

Caseless landmark names
Landmark names are unique per mission under Unicode canonical caseless matching with full case folding.

Forced colours on the disc
With forced colours active, the disc's track, lens, crosshair, pins and landmark marks are drawn in the current system colours and keep at least 3 to 1 contrast against the disc background.

Transactional outbox
A confirmed upload is marked `stored` and queued for parsing in one database transaction, and parse jobs and webhook sends reach the broker only through the outbox, as qualified in Services.

Queue topology
The parse and webhook exchanges and quorum queues exist with the names and arguments in Services, and every app instance consumes them with manual acknowledgement after its work commits.

Redelivered parses add nothing
A parse job delivered more than once, including after a crash or a second relay, adds no second sample, transcript line, search document, version increase, audit entry, webhook or push alert.

Parser failures dead-lettered
A capture the parser cannot finish is redelivered until the parse queue's delivery limit dead-letters it, and the pass then shows `rejected` with reason `parser_failed` and no line number.

Parse queue outage and recovery
With the parse queue unreachable, uploads still answer 202 and stay `stored` with the queued copy and banner, and when it answers again every waiting pass parses in upload order without a restart.

Reference ephemeris fetch
Setting a mission's reference target fetches every page of the ephemeris service's vectors for the mission's time span and stores them in metres, metres per second and Unix milliseconds, as qualified in Services.

Considerate ephemeris client
The ephemeris client honours `Retry-After` in both its forms, revalidates with `If-None-Match`, and never has more than one request in flight per mission across instances.

Ephemeris failures
An unknown target is refused with the field error in API and changes nothing, while a failing, slow or malformed ephemeris answer leaves the reference `unavailable` and everything else working.

Residuals
Each sample's residual is its distance from the reference position interpolated at its UTC, shown as the readout's `ΔR` line, the event list's residual column and the dossier's perilune lines, or as a dash where the reference has no value there.

Set a reference journey
The author types a reference target on the seeded mission, sees the reference become ready, and reads `ΔR` values on the readout that a freshly opened share page repeats.

Mission dossier
Both consoles download a mission dossier PDF rendered by the PDF renderer, A4 portrait, titled and named after the mission with RFC 6266 and RFC 8187 parameters, with the sections, order and display formats in Services and private notes only in the author dossier.

Text fields refuse control characters
Mission names, event titles, private notes and landmark names refuse control characters and line or paragraph separators with the published field error, and count their length in code points after NFC.

Renderer outage
With the PDF renderer unreachable or slower than 10 seconds, dossier requests answer the renderer outage status and the console announces the published copy, while everything else works.

Share rate limit
Each share link is limited to 120 requests in any rolling 60 seconds across all app instances, answering 429 with `Retry-After` and rate-limit fields beyond that, and serving without a limit while the cache is unreachable.

Live reader count
The author console's Share region shows how many share pages of the mission are open across all instances, updating within 5 seconds of a reader arriving or closing the page.

Released on close
Closing a share page, a stream or a download part-way releases its server work at once, leaving no database session active or idle in a transaction.

Archive plan billing
The Archive plan catalogue, the author's billing account and its subscription live in the billing system in decimal major units, while the app keeps integer cents and bytes and changes its plan only after billing confirms, as qualified in Services.

Archive plan display
The Missions page's Archive plan region shows each plan's price, the current quota, the bytes used, the next invoice date and the balance in the published formats.

Storage quota
An upload that would take the bytes of all non-deleted passes above the plan's quota is refused with `quota_exceeded`, reaching the quota exactly is allowed, and of simultaneous uploads near the limit only those that fit succeed.

Upgrade the Archive plan journey
The author is refused an upload over the free quota, upgrades to the 1 GiB plan on the Missions page, sees the price, quota, next invoice date and balance from billing, and the retried upload succeeds.

Mission subscribers
The author adds and removes up to three subscriber URLs per mission, each an endpoint of the mission's webhook application, with the answers in API.

Signed change webhooks
Each pinned event, parsed, rejected or deleted pass and revoked or replaced share link sends exactly one signed webhook whose event id is the mission and change version and whose payload never holds a note, relayed through the outbox and delivered once after a webhooks outage.

Parse outcome push alerts
Each parse outcome publishes exactly one push alert to the mission's topic with the title, message, priority, tags and click in Services, is never retried when push is unreachable, and is never sent for the seed pass.
`/app/run.json` exists with string `install`, `build` and `serve` fields and `"_schema":"run-manifest-v1"`, and nothing else is needed to install, build and serve the app.
`/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` names every shipped package (the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`) and every bundled font, each with its licence.

Every shipped package (the production dependency tree from `npm ls --omit=dev --all --json`) and every bundled font is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, Unicode-3.0 or SIL OFL 1.1.

The app keeps its own state only in the provided Postgres, MinIO, Meilisearch, RabbitMQ and Valkey (billing, webhook and push records live only in Kill Bill, Svix and ntfy), with no SQLite, no other database, cache or broker, and no captures or PDFs kept on the local disk.
The provided service definitions and their development credentials are left unchanged.
Application source, both server and browser, is TypeScript, and plain JavaScript appears only in tool configuration files.
Fonts, scripts and styles are bundled with the app, and no source file references a third-party origin.
